summary: An abstract class defines methods that every subclass must write, and you cannot create objects from it directly. Use one when several classes share a shape but compute something differently.
notes: Gradable(ABC) plus @abstractmethod makes percent() required in every concrete subclass.
Assignment inherits percent() as abstract, so it is still abstract even with __init__ and summary().
Python checks for missing abstract methods when you create the object, not when the file loads.
pitfall: Forgetting to write percent() in a subclass causes TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class Quiz without an implementation for abstract method 'percent'.
